details:
While the Steam Frame's design is to prioritize streaming PC VR, I feel like one of its biggest selling points was the fact that its hardware was designed to be performant enough to run PCVR games in standalone mode. It's one of the biggest reasons why they made the FEX translation layer; to allow games designed to run on x86 PCs to run on the Steam Frames ARM processor.

It has the specs to handle PCVR, in standalone mode. My PCVR streaming setup is on a budget gaming laptop with 16GB of LPDDR5 RAM, an intel i7-13620H CPU, and an NVIDIA RTX 4050 GPU. The Steam Frame's hardware (16GB LPDDR5X unified RAM, and Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 SoC) I could very much so believe could swing in the same performance bracket as my laptop, maybe even better.

My PCVR setup before this laptop was another budget gaming laptop from 2020, with 16GB LPDDR4, with an intel i7-10750H, and an NVIDIA RTX 2060.

The Steam Frame, I feel like, at bare minimum, should be allowed to attempt to run the PC version of VRChat in standalone, as it has the hardware for handling PCVR. Sure, it's not gonna be the same as if you had 64GB DDR5 with a 15900k and 5090, but I feel like it can likely handle it.

I have been in Club F.Y.Y.N. at Furality in 300 people instances on my laptop before, and while yeah, I had to have my culling insanely high, I was able to be there with largely decent framerates (30-40fps, maybe 50 at times), even able to show some peoples avatars. Instances with less than 20-30 people, unless the world is more intensive than average, I don't even need to have my avatar culling on.

To force the Steam Frame to only have access to the Android version of VRChat in standalone mode, I feel like largely defeats one of the biggest reasons to have a Steam Frame. If my goal was solely and exclusively a seamless PCVR streaming experience, I'd just stay on my Quest 3, or to get away from Meta, get one of the other cheaper standalone headsets, like something from Pico. Virtual Desktop is already a very smooth PC VR streaming experience. PC VR streaming in itself, has been a largely solved issue, and the Steam Frame, as a piece of hardware isn't game changing in that. If Valve's goal with the Steam Frame was exclusively to enable PC VR streaming, they could've just made the software, and released the Steam Frame's dongle, as something that could be used with other headsets, which also would have made the leaps and strides in PCVR streaming that have come with the software innovations from the Steam Frame's launch more accessible. Valve made a VR headset though that could compete with a PC in performance though, and it should be treated like one.

The Steam Deck can also run the PC version of VRChat, and the Steam Frame is, in many senses, just a VR version of the Steam Deck. To treat the Steam Frame, as another mobile headset defeats its purpose (which VRChat's mobile version was designed to be limited to Quest 2 levels of performance, leagues behind the Steam Frame's), is vastly limiting to the Steam Frame's use cases, and thus, the innovation of both VRChat and the VR industry, as a whole.

Let the Steam Frame, at least, have the option to run the PC version of VRChat in standalone mode.
title: Option for Steam Frame to run the PC Version of VRChat
